findings.title: Breaking API change: `findMany` removed and replaced with `getBaseConditions`
findings.body: The public method `findMany(findManyArgs)` has been removed and replaced with `getBaseConditions()` which returns raw SQL conditions instead of executing a query. Any existing callers of `service.findMany(...)` will break at compile time. The PR does not include updates to callers, so this is either an incomplete change or requires a coordinated update in consuming code.

findings.title: Dead code: `else if (filterConditions)` and `else` branches in `getBaseConditions` are unreachable
findings.body: `getAuthorizationConditions()` has return type `Promise<Prisma.Sql>` and always returns a `Prisma.Sql` object (including `NOTHING_CONDITION`), never null or undefined. Therefore `authConditions` is always truthy, making the `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else` branches unreachable dead code. While not a runtime bug, it misleads readers into thinking authorization conditions can be absent.

findings.title: Caching tests removed without replacement
findings.body: The previous test suite included tests verifying that `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` return cached results on repeated calls. These tests were removed entirely. Since the caching mechanism (`cachedAuthConditions`, `cachedFilterConditions`) still exists in the service, there is no test coverage ensuring it works correctly after the refactor, particularly that `Prisma.Sql` objects are cached and returned by reference or value consistently.

findings.title: Constructor type relaxed from strict discriminated union to loose public type
findings.body: The constructor parameter type changed from `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` (a strict zod-inferred discriminated union that requires `teamId` when `scope` is `"team"`) to `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` (which makes `teamId` optional for all scopes). While runtime validation via `safeParse` still catches invalid input, callers that previously got compile-time errors for missing `teamId` with team scope will now silently pass type-checking and receive `NOTHING_CONDITION` at runtime, potentially hiding integration bugs.

findings.title: Org scope includes org ID in team booking condition, which may match unintended bookings
findings.body: In `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition`, `teamIds` is constructed as `[options.orgId, ...teamsFromOrg.map(t => t.id)]` and used in `("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})) AND ("isTeamBooking" = true)`. This means bookings where `teamId` equals the org's own ID and `isTeamBooking` is true will match. If the org itself is not expected to have direct team bookings (only its child teams should), this could return unintended results. The old code had the same behavior, but this is worth verifying as part of the raw SQL conversion since the semantics are now more explicit.
